1. Introduction
ThegeologicrecordintheTianshanRangeatteststoacomplexhistoryofPaleozoicsubduction-relatedpro-
cesses [Burtman, 1975; Windley et al., 1990; Xiao et al., 2004] and a later phase of Cenozoic reactivation
inducedbycontinentalcollision[TapponnierandMolnar,1977,1979].Itisestimatedthat~40%ofthetotal
India-Asia convergence has been absorbed within the Tianshan [Abdrakhmatov et al., 1996; Reigber et al.,
2001; Wang et al., 2001], and as the most active intracontinental mountain belt in the world, this orogen
provides an outstanding natural laboratory for studying Cenozoic intracontinental deformation [Burchfiel
etal.,1999;Sobeletal.,2006;Sunetal.,2004].
TheTarimBasinisaforelandbasintotheTianshanwherethewesternsectorcomprisesthe~160kmlongby
70kmwideKashiDepression.ThisisoverthrustbytheNorthPamirThrustFault(NPTF)inthesouthandby
theSouthTianshanThrustFaultandtheKalpinUpliftinthenorth.Itcontainsmorethan6kmofNeogene
andQuaternarysediments[Heermanceetal.,2007]providingakeyopportunityforexaminingrelationships
betweensedimentationandtectonicdeformation.
Duringthepastseveraldecades,extensiveresearchhasbeenconductedtoconstrainthetimingoftectonic
deformation,uplift,andassociateddepositionlinkedtotheCenozoichistoryofTianshanorogenesis[Allen
etal.,1999;Avouacetal.,1993;Bullenetal.,2001;Burchfieletal.,1999;Chenetal.,2002;Heermanceetal.,
2007; Huanget al., 2006; Molnar and Tapponnier, 1975; Tapponnier and Molnar, 1979; Windley et al., 1990;
Yinetal.,1998;Zhang,2004].Thismultidisciplinaryresearchhasincludedinvestigationsofstructuralgeology,

demonstrated that the uplift chronology varies both from east to west and north to south across the
TianshanorogenwithregionalvariationsconstrainedwithintheintervalfromlateOligocenetomiddletolate
Miocenetimes[Abdrakhmatovetal.,1996;AmidonandHynek,2010;Bullenetal.,2001;Hendrixetal.,1994];a

etal.,2003].However,allresearchersrecognizethatthemostimportantphaseofupliftoccurredduringthe

ThickCenozoicterrigenousdepositsderivedmostlyfromtheupliftingmountainrangearewellpreserved
and exposed in the Kashi Depression [Charreau et al., 2009a; Chen et al., 2002; Hendrix et al., 1994; Yang
andLiu,2002;Huangetal.,2010]wherethedepositsdividebroadlyintolight-coloredfluviolacustrineoraeo-
liansediments,conglomerates,andredbeds[Li,1984;Yinetal.,1998].Thesefaciescontrastsareinterpreted

ofthesedimentaryrecord,reliablechronologicalcontrolisessential.However,continentaldepositstypically
lackdiagnosticfossilflorasandfaunas,andwhenthereisapaucityofdatablevolcanichorizons,magnetos-
tratigraphybecomesthekeytoolforcalibratingterrestrialdeposition[Chenetal.,2002;Huangetal.,2006].
ThistechniquehasalreadybeenappliedbyanumberofresearchgroupstoconstrainthehistoryofCenozoic
upliftintheTianshanregion[Charreauetal.,2005,2006,2009a;Chenetal.,2002;Huangetal.,2006;Jietal.,
2008;Sunetal.,2004,2005;Yangetal.,2015].Thesestudieshaverecognizedseveralpulsesofsedimentation
at~24Ma,~17–16Ma,~11Ma,~7Ma,and~4Mainterpretedtoreflectmultiplestagestotheorogenicuplift
[Bullenetal.,2001;Charreauetal.,2005,2006;Huangetal.,2006;Jietal.,2008;Luetal.,2010;Sunetal.,2004,
2009].Theexpandingnumberofmagnetostratigraphicresultshasalsodemonstratedadiachronousupliftin
the Tianshan, while interregional comparisons have highlighted chronological problems particularly con-
cerningthetimingofcoarseclasticinputathigherlevelsofthesuccession[Yangetal.,2015].
ThispaperreportsanewpaleomagneticstudyfromtheMio-Plioceneforelandbasinsuccessioninthesouth-
westernTianshan.ThestudiedlocalitiesareinthevicinityofthetownofJiashiwherethisbasinalsequenceis
composedof~9kmofCenozoicsediments[Chenetal.,2002;Heermanceetal.,2007]withimportantpotential
fordocumentingthetectonicanderosionalhistoriesofthesouthwesternTianshan[Jiaetal.,2004;Zhouand
Chen,1990].Theserocksarenowfoldedintoasuiteofelongateopenanticlinesandsynclinesthuspermitting
applicationof thepaleomagneticfoldtest.In theeventthepaleomagneticinvestigationyieldsa detailed
chronologicalcontrolforthethickCenozoicdepositsinthisregionandprovidesanexpandedbasisfordis-
cussingtheuplifthistoryoftheTianshanMountainssincethemid-Miocene.Aspartofthisstudy,wealso
includeanewbasalageestimatefortheXiyuFormationanddiscussthetectonicandclimaticsignificance
ofthiscoarseclasticfacies.
2. Geological Setting,Paleomagnetic Sampling,andMethods
ThesouthernTianshan-northernTarimisanoutstandingexampleofactiveintracontinentalthrustingand
coupled sedimentation wherestructures and sediment thickness variations in theforeland basin reflect a
strong control by deformation style imparted by the adjacent thrust system [Allen et al., 1999] (Figure 1).
The Neogene strata deposited within the Kashi Depression are comprehensively reviewed in a range of
papersinbothChineseandEnglishwhichprovidethebasisforthisstudy[BureauofGeologyandMineral
ResourcesofXinjiangAutonomousRegion(BGMRXUAR),1993;Chenetal.,2002,2007;Heermanceetal.,2007,
2008;Huangetal.,2009;Jiaetal.,2004;Schareretal.,2004;Yinetal.,1998;Zhou,2001].Thepresentinvestiga-
tion is concerned with that part of the succession formed during the Late Cenozoic era exposed in the
Dashankousection(Figure2).
TheNeogenesequenceinthissectionisentirelyterrestrialinoriginandcomprises,inascendingorder,the
Wuqia Group, the Atushi Formation, and the largely conglomeratic Xiyu Formation [BGMRXUAR, 1993;
Heermanceetal.,2007,2008;Huangetal.,2009;Jiaetal.,2004].ThehigherpartoftheWuqiaGroupiscom-
posedofthePakabulakaFormationconsistingofthick-beddedandmassivesandstoneswithredbrownto
dark mudstones interbedded with sandy mudstones. These contain foraminifers, ostracods, chareae, and
sporopollen [Jia et al., 2004; Zheng et al., 1999]. The formation is locally gypsiferous and is interpreted to

4. Correlation Withthe GTS2012
DirectionsoftheChRMsfromthe985horizonshavebeenusedtocalculatevirtualgeomagneticpole(VGP)
latitudesandthesampledsectionorganizedintostratigraphiclevelsreferredtotheVGPlatitudesinorderto
define magnetic polarity zones (Figure 7). The gypsum-bearing Pakabulake Formation is assigned to the
Serravallianstage[Heermanceetal.,2007]onthebasisoftheoccurrenceofafaunacomprisingOstracoda
assemblagesincludingEucyprisinsolitaJiang,Eucypriscf.longaMandelstam,DarwinulaignobilisJiang,and
CyprinotousoptalusJiang.Wethereforeconsiderthatdepositionofthesuccessionstudiedherecommenced
inthemid-Miocene.Zhengetal.[2000]findthattheAtushiFormationintheKashiDepressionisdominated
by a long reversed polarity zone presumed to correlate with the Gilbert reversed chron, while in the
Kepintage anticline, Zhou and Chen [1990] find assemblages through the correlative stratigraphic interval
oftheAtushiindicatingaPlioceneage;thesetwolinesofevidenceprovideachronostratigraphiccontrol
for the higher levels of the present study. We therefore correlate the underlying Atushi Formation in the
DashankousectiontochronsC3rtoC2Arimplyingabasalageof~6.0Ma(Figure7).Giventheobservation
that Xiyu conglomerate has generally prograded southward [Chen et al., 2002, 2007; Heermance et al.,
2007],weexpecttheDashankousectiontoincorporateaslightlyoldertimeintervalthanthesectionsstudied
byChenetal.[2002].Unfortunately,thelowerpartofourpolaritysequence,whichischaracterizedbyamixed
polarityzonebelow~500m,precedesarelativelylongreversalzoneat520–680mandweareunabletocor-
relatethisfirmlywiththeGTS2012[Gradsteinetal.,2012].Thereareseveralpossibleexplanationsforthis
including (i) variable rates of sedimentation prevailing during early stages of the infilling of the foreland
basin,(ii)possibleoverlappingortruncationofthesection byunidentifiedfaulting,or(iii)aninfluenceof
the tectonically induced magnetic fabric recognized by the anisotropy of magnetic susceptibility (AMS)
study.Weconsiderthat(i)istheonlyplausibleexplanationbecause(ii)isunlikelyinthecontextofcareful
fieldobservation,while(iii)canbeessentiallydismissedbecausethefabricissoweakthatitcannotsignifi-
cantlyhaveaffectedthedirectionalresults.Hence,wefavor(i)andproposeacorrelationofthismixedpolar-
ityzonewithchronsC5Ar.1rtoC5ADnoftheGTS2012(Figure7)toconcludethattheDashankousectionwas
depositedbetweenapproximately~12.4Maand~3.0Ma(i.e.,itismid-MiocenetolatePlioceneinage).
Theplotofmagnetostratigraphicageversusstratigraphicthicknesswithinthecompositesectionisshownin

to~34.5cm/yrat6.73Ma.Thiscorrespondsinagetothefourthofthefivepulsesofsedimentationrecog-

5. Anisotropy of MagneticSusceptibility (AMS) Results
AMSprovidesameasureofrockfabricthatcanpotentiallyresultfromdepositionalorpostdepositionalsedi-
mentaryfactors,oracombinationofboth[Channelletal.,1979],oritmayalternativelyrecordtheimprintof
latertectonism.Whentherelativecontributionsoftheseeffectscanbeisolatedinthecontextoftheregional
geologicalhistory,AMScanpotentiallyyieldinformationtohelpunderstandthepaleogeographicevolution
ofasedimentarybasin[MarinoandEllwood,1978].
InthisstudyAMStensorswereresolvedbyapplicationofaKLY-4Kappabridgesusceptibilitymeteranddeter-
mined for 985 specimens. The results identify significant changes with lithology and stratigraphic position
through the section (Figure 9). Specifically, bulk magnetic susceptibility is lowest (with an average value of
249.9μSI)nearthebaseofthesuccession.Thisisfollowedbya3.5Mainterval(~11–7.5Ma)ofcontinuinglow
valuesbelow400μSI.By~7.5Ma(the1650mlevelinthesuccession)k showssignificantincreasetoarelatively
m
highermeanvalueof352.8μSIuntil~3.6Ma(the2940mlevel);k increasesandremainshighthereafter.The
m
overall relatively weak values of bulk susceptibility (mostly <400μSI) indicate that anisotropic paramagnetic
andantiferromagneticmineralssuchastheclaysandhematitepredominantlycontrolboththesusceptibility
andanisotropyofthesesediments[TarlingandHrouda,1993].However,thenotableincreaseofk abovethe
m
~2940mlevelmaybeduetoincreasedinputofsmallamountsofmagnetiteafter~3.6Ma(section6.1).

6. Discussion
6.1. BasalAgeoftheXiyuConglomerates
TheXiyuconglomerateswerefirstdescribedbyObruchevinthe1930s.Later,T.K.Huangdescribedthelithol-
ogiesinmoredetailandassignedtheconglomeratestoaXiyuFormation.AsoriginallyproposedbyHuang
etal.[1947]inthenorthernTianshan,thisassignationdescribedasuiteoftypicallymassive,50to3200m
thick,molassicdepositscomprisingdarkgraypebbletoboulderconglomerateswithclastsizesrangingfrom
3to>30cm;minorinterbedsofmudstoneorsandstoneoccurwherethegradationalbasedefinestheregio-
nal increase in sedimentation rate. Huanget al. [1947] extended this description to cover a coherent and
quasi-continuousunitlyingatthetopofthesedimentarypileinmanyofthecentralAsianforelandbasins.
TherearetwoopposingexplanationsforthesedimentarytransitiondefinedbytheXiyuFormation,namely,
(i)thesemassiveconglomeratesarethesignatureofalatemajorupliftoftheorogenyinresponsetoconti-
nuingimpingementofIndiaintoAsia[Charreauetal.,2009b;Huangetal.,1947,2010;Zhengetal.,2000]or
alternatively,(ii)thiscoarseclasticinputwascausedbyanincreaseinerosionratesresultingfromclimate
change[Burchfieletal.,1999;Sunetal.,2004,2007;Zhangetal.,2001].BecausetheXiyuFormationcannot
bedirectlydated,thebasalagesassignedintheTianshanregionhavesometimesreflectedprejudicescon-
cerningthesetwopossibleexplanations.
The succession studied here is located in a N-S trending outcrop belt crossing the southern limb of the
KepingtageAnticlineandlies~70kmeastoftheBoguzihesectionstudiedbyChenetal.[2002,Figure1].
Thestrata are laterally continuous and can be traced through to theBoguzihesection wherethebase of
theXiyuFormationisestimatedtorangefrom2.8MaonthenorthwestlimboftheAtushi-Talangheanticline
to1.9Maonthesouthwestlimb[Chenetal.,2002,Figure1].However,ourdatingofthemagnetostratigraphy
intheDashankousectionyieldsanageof~3.6Maforthisboundaryandsupportsthefindingoftheearlier
workersthattheXiyuFormationisdiachronousandyoungtowardthesouth[Chenetal.,2002;Heermance
etal.,2007].ThisdiachronouscharacteroftheXiyuFormationintheKashiareaisthereforelikelytohave
beenaconsequenceofpenecontemporaneousupliftresultinginrepeatedreworkingofmaterialdegraded
from the orogen and consequent progradation of sedimentary input into the foreland basin [Heermance
etal.,2007].
However,ifthedepositionofthisformationhadbeentheresultofachangeintheclimaticregimeacontem-
poraneousonsetofdepositionshouldberecognizedregionallyinlatePliocenetimesataround~2.6Main
NWChina[Sunetal.,2004,2007].Thisissuecanbefurtherevaluatedfromthestudyofrockmagneticpara-
metersbecausethesetendtoreflectthechangingbalanceofphysicaltochemicalweatheringprocessesas
theyrespondtodegreesofaridificationandcoolinginthesourceregion[Balsametal.,2004].Huangetal.
[2010] have shown that the climate changes suggested by rock magnetic properties in the Yaha section
do indeed correlate with the climate record in the neighboring Kuitun He on the northern piedmont
oftheTianShan[Sunetal.,2007].ContactsbetweentheXiyuconglomeratesandunderlyingstratainboth
theYahaandKuitunHesectionsandthecontrastingageestimatesfortheXiyuconglomeratesshowthat
the essential signature of this formation is independent of wider global climatic changes. Nevertheless,
climaticinfluenceswillnodoubthavemodulatedlocalsedimentaccumulationratesandtheimpactofthe
Plio-PleistoceneclimatictransitionontheNeogenerecordoforogenyincentralAsiaremainsatopicofcon-
tinuingdebate.
6.2. ImplicationsfortheUpliftHistoryoftheSouthernTianshan
TheKapingtage(Kalpin)thrustzoneisanactivelydeformingpartoftheIndia-Asiacollisionsystemandlies
south of the Tianshan where it comprises a succession of emergent imbricate structures of arcuate form
(Figure 1). This thrust zone is the only margin of the Tarim Basin emplaced as a décollement in the
Cenozoic,andbothNeogeneandQuaternarystrataareobservedtobefoldedabovethefootwall.Inthevici-
nityofourstudyregiontheseemergentthrustsheetsvergemostlytowardtheinterioroftheTarimBasinto
thesouth;theyshownomajorinternaldeformationandhavesmoothlysigmoidalprofileswithdipsranging
typicallyfrom~20°to~45°[Allenetal.,1999].
ThetimingoftheonsetofCenozoicdeformationintheKepingtagethrustzoneisindicatedbythechangeof
sediment accumulation rate, a change correlating with a transition from lacustrine to alluvial facies in
Messiniantimesatabout6.7MaintheDashankousection[Jiaetal.,2004;Zhengetal.,1999].Asillustrated
QIAOETAL. MAGNETOSTRATIGRAPHYOFKASHIDEPRESSION 13

### page_14
Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth 10.1002/2015JB012687
inFigure8,theincreaseinsedimentationratefrom~24.8cm/yrto~34.5cm/yratthistimeisabruptandalso
correlateswithinputofconglomeratesinthesectionnearDushanziinthenorthernTianshanmountains[Sun
etal.,2004].ItisfurtherrecognizedbyamarkedincreaseinsedimentationrateinboththeKucheDepression
inthesouthernTianshanmountains[Huangetal.,2006;Jingetal.,2011]andintheJingouriversectionatthe
southernmarginoftheJunggarBasin[Jietal.,2008].
BecausetheTarimBasinisenclosed,thesedimentaccumulationratesarecontrolledprimarilybyratesof
sediment supply and the accommodation space. Sediment supply is a function of climate [Molnar, 2004],
sourcerocklithology[Carrolletal.,2006]andproximitytothesedimentsource[BurbankandBeck,1991].
The accommodation space is created either by tectonically induced subsidence beneath a faulted block
[Beaumont, 1981] or by uplift that serves to trap sedimentation within a Piggyback Basin [DeCelles and
Giles,1996].Thus,anabruptchangeinthesedimentaccumulationratecouldbetheresultofeitherachange
insedimentflux[Molnar,2001;Zhangetal.,2001]ortectonicsubsidence[Paolaetal.,1992]orbyacombina-
tion of both. Balanced section restoration of compressional deformation in the Kalpin Uplift has yielded
an estimate for a minimum shortening of ~22–28% during the late Cenozoic [Allen et al., 1999; Yin et al.,
1998],basedonthefieldobservationsandreconstructedcrosssections.Wethereforeinterpretthechange
insedimentationrateat6.7MaasatectonicallyinfluencedphenomenalinkedtotheKalpinUplift.
Moreover,thedramaticfaciesandsedimentationratechangesatthistimecouldalsoreflectthrustloadingin
thesouthernTianshan.Thus,aspointedoutbyJordanetal.[1988],anincreaseintheinputofsedimentstoa
foreland basin may or may not be related to thrusting, depending on whether climate conditions were
changing to increase or decrease the power of erosion. However, the relative contributions of tectonics
and climate to the erosion processes are still a subject of controversy [Burbank et al., 2003, 1993; Molnar
andEngland,1990;Sunetal.,2004].ClimaterecordsinbothwestAntarctica[KennettandBarker,1990]and
theArctic[ThiedeandVorren,1994]indicatecoolingandicesheetexpansionafter6Ma,andstablecarbon
isotopicstudiesoffossilsoilsfromPakistanandNorthAmericarevealanexpansionofC grassesat8–6Ma
4
indicatingthedevelopmentofanaridclimatecommencinginthelateMiocene[Cerlingetal.,1993].Given
thatthestudiedsectionislocatedinaregionofactivetectonics,theincreaseinabundanceofthearidspecies
ofArtemisiaandChenopodiaceaeafter6MaintheTaxihesection[SunandZhang,2008]mayhaveresulted
fromupliftofthemountainrangecausingittoactasabarriertotheinfluenceoftheIndianandpossiblyalso
theAtlanticOceansontheclimateofthecontinentalinterior.Althoughclimaticchangesnodoubtoccurred
duringdepositionoftheDashankousection,weconsiderthatthefacieschangeisprimarilyaresponsetolate
tectonicreactivationintheTianshan.
7. Conclusion
ThedetailedpaleomagneticstudyoftheDashankousectionhasprovidedahigh-resolutionchronologyfor
theNeogenesequenceintheKashiDepressioninthesouthwestpartoftheTianshanMountains.Onthebasis
ofthechrondurationsandOstracodaassemblagesfoundinthissection,ourpreferredmagnetostratigraphic
correlationsuggeststhatthesampled3187mthicksectionwasdepositedbetween~12.4Maand~3.0Ma,
i.e., middle Miocene (Serravallian) and late Pliocene times. A rapid increase in sedimentation rate at
~6.7Ma is interpreted to record onset of rejuvenated uplift of the Tianshan Mountains. While climatic
changesmayhavemodulatedthesedimentaryrecord,theydonotappeartobeadominantcontrolonsedi-
mentaccumulationbetween7.0and2.58Ma.Magneticfabricsidentifytheinfluenceoftheregionalstress
fieldimpartedbyongoingIndia-Asiacollisioninthelowerpartofthesuccessioncontrastingwithadominant
sedimentaryfabricpreservedinthehigherpartsofthesuccession.Togetherwithothermagnetostratigraphic
